title: MA7-09234
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: INTRODUCTION [1] The claimant is Ms. XXXX XXXX who is a 59 year old citizen of Pakistan. Ms. XXXX is seeking protection in Canada citing Sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

Ms. XXXX alleges that because of her faith, which is Ahmadi Muslim, she has been targeted by 'XXXX' XXXX XXX who is an extremist XXXX at a nearby Mosque and XXXX of the local Aahafaz Khateme Nabuwat organization. This organization has a history of targeting and persecuting Ahmadi Muslims.

The claimant alleges that she regularly hosted 'events' at her house. For example, she would have local woman over to XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX. Ms. XXXX also alleges that she was appointed 'XXXX XXXX' of her local Jamaat's Lajna (Ahmadi Women's Organization) and therefore she was involved in XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX.

The claimant alleges that in XXXX 2007 Mr. XXX mentioned the claimant XXXX XXXX. Mr. XXX charged the claimant with "actively organising Ahmadi religious activities in my house and was teaching Quran (Ahmadi version) to Sunni children". The next week the claimant alleges that four of Mr. XXX's "hooligans" damaged her satellite dish. The claimant asked for police help but when they discovered that the claimants were Ahmadi they determined that it was a religious problem and they refused to help.

Soon the claimant was receiving threatening phone calls and some of the claimant's friends were harassed. The claimant was then personally threatened by Mr. XXXX. The most serious incident occurred on XXXX, 2007 when the claimant had XX women at her house for an annual Lajna Tarbyati meeting. XXXX XXXX XXX with several followers protested outside and the woman needed to be escorted home for their own protection. According to the claimant, "XXXX verbally announced death verdict against me". The claimant then hid in another part of XXXX. After consideration the claimant fled Pakistan to arrive in Canada on the advice of her husband.

The panel determines that Ms. XXXX is not a "convention refugee" under section 96 of IRPA. The claimant is also not a person "in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97(1)(a) or (b) of IRPA.
The panel is satisfied as to the identity of the claimant. The panel was provided a passport and marriage certificate for review.
With respect to credibility the panel does not find the claimant is telling the truth. There are aspects of the claim which are vague or lacking in plausibility. At times the claimant was evasive.

The basic allegation that the claimant was targeted by 'XXXX' XXXX XXX is possible. At the same time there are numerous indicators that the claim is a fabrication. To begin with, before the claimant arrived in Canada, CIC received information from the claimant's former son in law that the claimant was planning to make a refugee claim in Canada. According to Mr. XXXX XXXX XXXX the claimant was going to "apply the visit visa for Canada and upon arrival here in Canada she will apply for asylum (refugee) for getting immigration, as they plan together".1 This communication was received on XXXX, 2006.

In fact the claimant did not claim refugee status after arrival in Canada in XXXX 2006. The claimant stayed in Canada for 4 months and returned to Pakistan in XXXX. The claimant alleges, however, that upon return to Pakistan she was soon being targeted by Mr. XXX and as a result, on her return to Canada in XXXX 2007, she did make a refugee claim.

When questioned on why Mr. XXXX would attempt to predict the claimant's behaviour (the refugee claim) the claimant argues that Mr. XXXX was resentful over the failed marriage with her daughter. The claimant states that he was "lying" about what the claimant said and the claimant argues that because she in fact returned to Pakistan in 2006 provides evidence of this. The panel concludes that although a marriage breakdown may create animosity, this does not detract from the fact that Mr. XXXX was essentially correct in his prediction.

The claimant was asked to provide any evidence of the existence of Mr. XXX. The claimant could not. Her basic answer to the repeated question if she had any proof of the existence of Mr. XXX was that no one was even allowed in his Mosque. In addition, the claimant was very vague on the location of Mr. XXX's mosque. The claimant gave a confused answer. The claimant stated that Mr. XXX's Mosque was in the XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX but was evasive about the specific location speaking first about it being in an adjacent town then about it being in a 'border' area. The claimant could also not give the name of the Mosque where Mr. XXX XXXX.

Panel does not find these answers satisfactory. The claimant has lived in this house in XXX since 1996. The claimant is an educated woman from a family of professionals. She has access to financial resources. Regardless, the claimant has provided no documentary evidence of the existence of Mr. XXX or of any of the events described.

The claimant was also vague about her involvement in the Lajna organization. When asked about how she got the position of 'XXXX XXXX' in her local Lajna, she states that the president appointed her. At the same time the claimant could only identify the president by a first name. The claimant also states that during the one year period that she returned to Pakistan there was more than one president but she didn't know the names of the other presidents. The claimant also appears to lack knowledge of organizational activities of the Lajna. Aside from the Treasurer, President and XXXX XXXX, the claimant could not name another job or office in the organization. The claimant could not name other members of the organization or even give the names of individuals who were at her house on XXXX, 2007 when her house was allegedly attacked by Mr. XXX and his supporters.

The panel also notes that the claimant's status as an 'XXXX XXXX' is first mentioned in an amendment to the PIF Narrative received in XXXX 2008. The original PIF narrative gives a rendition of events which implies that the claimant was not involved in any structured events. According to the claimant: The monthly gathering of the Lajna (Ahmadi women organization) was a regular event at my house XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
The claimant did not provide a response to the question of why there was no prior mention of her official role in the Lajna in the Port of Entry documentation or the PIF Narrative.

In addition the panel also finds it implausible that the claimant could not receive some form of police protection. The area that the claimant lived in is a very prosperous area and the security is provided by the military. The claimant's husband is a retired XXXX in the military and one of her sons is an active service XXXX stationed in XXXX.

Furthermore, according to the brochure promoting sales of new properties in the area, "Home to many, XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXX) is a residential Paradise, a cultural heartland and a land of endless opportunities... XXX XXXX is a home to world class universities, schools, mosques, hospitals, commercial centers, parks and above all, a secure idyllic community."2 With respect to where the claimant lives in XXX, there is a police station at the end of the block.3 From the appearance of XXX this does not appear to be a place where a religious extremist and 'hooligans' would be allowed to do as they please in terms of roughing up citizens, damaging private property (damage to the satellite dish) and protesting in the neighborhood.

In addition, the actions of the claimant's family strongly suggest that this area is free of such danger. To begin with the claimant's son along with his wife and family continued to live in the house after the claimant fled. There are also servants who have lived continuously at the house. The claimant's husband also lives there when he is in XXXX. The claimant's daughter, XXXX, who was formally in Canada and with whom the claimant was living, has returned to Pakistan and lives in the house. The claimant was asked why her daughter returned to Pakistan. The claimant replied that she wanted to see her friends again and was bored. Although Mr. XXX is focused on the claimant the fact remains that the claimant was targeted partly because she is Ahmadi. Yet the behaviour of this family, aside from the claimant, suggests that there is a substantial degree of security at this house.

The panel notes that all of the claimant's family members are educated and professional. The claimant's husband is a retired XXXX who possesses a BSc. and a law degree. The claimant's eldest son, XXXX possesses an MBA and works for XXXX. The claimant's middle son, XXXX is an army XXXX. The claimant's youngest son, who lives at the house but is between jobs, has an MBA. The claimant's husband mostly lives in his home village of origin. At the same time the claimant states that her husband has family members living there and properties which provide him revenue. The claimant's husband also has people cooking and cleaning for him there. All this indicates that the family as a whole is prosperous and secure.
Taken together the panel determines that on a balance of probabilities the allegations of the claimant are false.

For all of the reasons set out above this panel determines that the claimant is not a 'convention refugee' nor is she a 'person in need of protection' therefore the claim is denied. Stephen J. Gallagher Stephen J.
